name: bare-signals

exports.name: Signal
signatures:
interface Signal {
  start(): this
  stop(): this
  ref(): this
  unref(): this
  close(): Promise<void>
  addListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  addOnceListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  prependListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  prependOnceListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  removeListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  removeAllListeners<E extends keyof M>(name?: E): this
  on<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  once<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  off<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  emit<E extends keyof M>(name: E, ...args: M[E]): boolean
  listeners<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E): EventHandler<M[E], R>
  rawListeners<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E): EventHandler<M[E], R>[]
  eventNames(): (keyof M)[]
  listenerCount<E extends keyof M>(name: E): number
  getMaxListeners(): number
  setMaxListeners(n: number): void
}
exports.description: A native OS signal that can be listened for, started, stopped, and closed.

members.name: Signal
members.description: Create a `Signal` for `signum`, given as a signal number or name such as `'SIGINT'`. Throws if `signum` is a string that names an unknown signal.

members.name: close
members.description: Close the signal, releasing its underlying handle. Returns a promise that resolves once the `close` event has fired.

members.name: ref
members.description: Ref the signal, keeping the event loop alive while it is active.

members.name: Signal.constants
members.description: The map of known signal names to signal numbers.

members.name: start
members.description: Start listening for the signal, emitting `signal` when it is received. Throws if the signal has been closed.

members.name: unref
members.description: Unref the signal, allowing the event loop to exit even while it is active.

exports.name: SignalEmitter

interface SignalEmitter {
  ref(): this
  unref(): this
  addListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  addOnceListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  prependListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  prependOnceListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  removeListener<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  removeAllListeners<E extends keyof M>(name?: E): this
  on<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  once<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  off<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E, fn: EventHandler<M[E], R>): this
  emit<E extends keyof M>(name: E, ...args: M[E]): boolean
  listeners<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E): EventHandler<M[E], R>
  rawListeners<E extends keyof M, R>(name: E): EventHandler<M[E], R>[]
  eventNames(): (keyof M)[]
  listenerCount<E extends keyof M>(name: E): number
  getMaxListeners(): number
  setMaxListeners(n: number): void
}
exports.description: An `EventEmitter` that lazily starts and stops a `Signal` for each named signal as listeners are added and removed, emitting the signal name and number.

members.name: ref
members.description: Ref all currently tracked signals, keeping the event loop alive.

members.name: unref
members.description: Unref all currently tracked signals, allowing the event loop to exit.

exports.name: SignalError
exports.description: An error thrown by `bare-signals`, such as for an unknown signal name or an operation on a closed signal.

members.name: code
members.description: The error code, such as `UNKNOWN_SIGNAL` or `SIGNAL_CLOSED`.
